Python: saving and predicting

Source: vignettes/articles/python-prediction.Rmd
python-prediction.Rmd

Checkpoints, what they record about the run, and predictions for new plots: the predictor, its predictions, retrieval of the nearest training plots, the scalers, the run record, and the helpers that rebuild a checkpoint’s loader settings and targets.

All of the Python reference

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/resolve/r")

# The engine library, downloaded once
library(resolveR)
resolve.install_backend()
pip install resolve-core

The examples on this page run in order on the survey that ships with the R package: 150 plots in the Alps, with one table of plots and one of the species recorded on them. They start from a short fit saved as a checkpoint; Predicting new plots walks through the same steps with their output.

import os
import tempfile

import pandas as pd
import resolve_core as rc

data = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gcol33/resolve/master/r/inst/extdata/"
plots = pd.read_csv(data + "plots.csv")
species = pd.read_csv(data + "species.csv")

roles = rc.RoleMapping()
roles.plot_id = "plot_id"
roles.species_id = "species"
roles.abundance = "cover"
roles.genus = "genus"
roles.family = "family"
targets = [rc.TargetSpec.regression("elevation"),
           rc.TargetSpec.classification("habitat", 4)]
dataset = rc.ResolveDataset.from_pandas(plots, species, roles, targets)

config = rc.TrainConfig()
config.max_epochs = 100
trainer = rc.Trainer(rc.ResolveModel(dataset.schema), config)
trainer.prepare_data(dataset)
trainer.fit()

folder = tempfile.mkdtemp()
path = os.path.join(folder, "model.pt")
trainer.save(path, metadata=trainer.run_metadata)

Predictor 

Predictor.load(path, device="cpu", vram_fraction=1.0)
Predictor(model, scalers, device="cpu")

Predictions from a trained model. load reads a checkpoint Trainer.save wrote; device is "cpu", "cuda" (the current GPU) or "cuda:N", and anything else raises ValueError. The checkpoint is read onto that device, so one trained on a GPU loads on a machine without one. vram_fraction caps the share of GPU memory the predictor may use. A file that cannot be read raises StorageError after a few retries; an unreadable archive raises RuntimeError. The constructor assembles a predictor from a model and its Scalers.

predictor = rc.Predictor.load(path)
predictor.schema.n_species_vocab

predict_dataset() 

predict_dataset(dataset, return_latent=False, batch_size=4096)

The predictions for every plot of a dataset, as ResolvePredictions. The dataset has to be coded with the checkpoint’s vocabularies, or its integer codes would index the wrong rows of the embedding tables: load new plots with ResolveDataset.from_csv_with_vocabs (or another *_with_vocabs loader), passing predictor.external_vocabs and predictor.dataset_config. A dataset coded any other way is refused. return_latent also returns each plot’s latent representation. batch_size is the number of plots per forward pass, -1 for one pass over the whole dataset; the outputs are moved to the CPU as each chunk is done, and the result does not depend on the chunk size.

plots.head(20).to_csv(os.path.join(folder, "new_plots.csv"), index=False)
species.to_csv(os.path.join(folder, "new_species.csv"), index=False)
new_plots = rc.ResolveDataset.from_csv_with_vocabs(
    os.path.join(folder, "new_plots.csv"),
    os.path.join(folder, "new_species.csv"),
    roles, [], predictor.external_vocabs, predictor.dataset_config)
preds = predictor.predict_dataset(new_plots)
preds.predictions["elevation"][:5]

predict() 

predict(*, coordinates=None, covariates=None, unknown_fraction=None,
        unknown_count=None, hash_embedding=None, genus_ids=None,
        family_ids=None, species_ids=None, species_vector=None,
        pool_genus_ids=None, pool_family_ids=None, pool_weights=None,
        pool_mask=None, pool_has_cover=None, categorical_ids=None,
        return_latent=False, batch_size=4096)

The predictions from tensors, every argument by keyword; leave out what the encoding does not use. The first five are the parts of the continuous block, assembled and standardised as in training; unknown_fraction and unknown_count are required where the model reads them. The other inputs are the ResolveDataset tensors of the same names. batch_size chunks the forward as in predict_dataset.

from_tensors = predictor.predict(
    unknown_fraction=new_plots.unknown_fraction,
    hash_embedding=new_plots.hash_embedding,
    genus_ids=new_plots.genus_ids, family_ids=new_plots.family_ids)

Embeddings

  • get_embeddings(*, ..., batch_size=4096): each plot’s latent representation, (n_plots, latent_dim), from the keyword inputs of predict.
  • get_species_embeddings(): the species table, (n_species_vocab, species_embed_dim), or None for the hash and sparse encodings.
  • get_genus_embeddings(), get_family_embeddings(): the genus and family tables, or None without taxonomy.

The tables come back detached, on the CPU. Latent and species embeddings reads them.

latent = predictor.get_embeddings(
    unknown_fraction=new_plots.unknown_fraction,
    hash_embedding=new_plots.hash_embedding,
    genus_ids=new_plots.genus_ids, family_ids=new_plots.family_ids)
latent.shape

set_retrieval() 

set_retrieval(reference, config=RetrievalConfig(), batch_size=4096)
clear_retrieval()

Retrieval augmentation (Gorishniy and others 2024, TabR): every later prediction is blended with the labels of the plot’s nearest reference plots in the latent space. reference is a dataset coded with the checkpoint’s vocabularies and carrying every target’s labels, normally the training plots; target_specs_from_schema gives its targets. For each plot the k_neighbors reference plots of highest cosine similarity of their latents are weighted by a softmax of similarity over temperature. Only neighbours labelled for a target count for it, and a plot with none keeps the model’s prediction. A regression target becomes (1 - alpha) * prediction + alpha * the neighbours' weighted label, in original units; a classification target blends its probabilities with the neighbours’ label distribution and predicts the largest. The latent and get_embeddings are not blended. The search is exact. A reference plot that is also scored finds itself first. clear_retrieval returns to the model’s own predictions.

reference = rc.ResolveDataset.from_pandas(plots, species, roles,
                                          rc.target_specs_from_schema(predictor.schema),
                                          predictor.dataset_config,
                                          schema_source=dataset)
retrieval = rc.RetrievalConfig()
retrieval.k_neighbors = 16
predictor.set_retrieval(reference, retrieval)
blended = predictor.predict_dataset(new_plots)
predictor.clear_retrieval()

optimize_for_inference() 

optimize_for_inference()

Folds the batch-normalisation layers into the linear layers before them. Call it after loading and before a large prediction run.

Attributes

  • model (ResolveModel), scalers (Scalers), schema (ResolveSchema) and device (str).
  • external_vocabs (ExternalVocabs): every training vocabulary, the categorical codes included, for the *_with_vocabs loaders.
  • dataset_config (DatasetConfig): the loader settings the checkpoint was trained under (dataset_config_from_checkpoint).
  • categorical_vocab (CategoricalVocab), species_vocab, genus_vocab, family_vocab (list[str], "<UNK>" first).
  • retrieval (RetrievalConfig or None) and n_retrieval_reference (int): the active retrieval and the size of its reference set.

ResolvePredictions

What predict_dataset and predict return.

  • predictions (dict[str, Tensor]): one entry per target. A regression target is in its original units, a Log1p target inverted. A classification target is an int64 class code, indexing the target’s class_names in predictor.schema.targets.
  • probabilities (dict[str, Tensor]): one (n_plots, n_classes) entry per classification target, column j the probability of code j; each row sums to one and its largest entry is the predicted code. Regression targets have no entry.
  • targets (dict[str, Tensor]): the recorded values, where the dataset carried them.
  • plot_ids (list[str]): the plot identifiers, in row order.
  • latent (Tensor or None): (n_plots, latent_dim) with return_latent=True.

A per-plot confidence comes from the probabilities alone: the largest probability, the margin between the two largest, or the entropy.

probs = preds.probabilities["habitat"]
confidence = probs.max(dim=1).values
top2 = probs.topk(2, dim=1).values
margin = top2[:, 0] - top2[:, 1]

habitat = next(t for t in predictor.schema.targets if t.name == "habitat")
table = pd.DataFrame({"plot_id": preds.plot_ids,
                      "elevation": preds.predictions["elevation"].numpy()})
table["habitat"] = [habitat.class_names[c] for c in preds.predictions["habitat"]]
for j, name in enumerate(habitat.class_names):
    table[f"habitat_prob_{name}"] = probs[:, j].numpy()

RetrievalConfig 

RetrievalConfig()

The settings of Predictor.set_retrieval: k_neighbors (int, default 96), the reference plots each prediction reads; alpha (float, default 0.3), the neighbours’ share of the blend; temperature (float, default 1.0), of the softmax over cosine similarity. validate() raises for a value out of range.

nearest_by_cosine() 

nearest_by_cosine(queries, reference, k, exclude_self=False)

The search set_retrieval runs, on any rows: for each row of queries, the k rows of reference most similar to it by cosine similarity, most similar first. Both are dense (rows, dim) tensors of one dim; a numpy array goes through torch.from_numpy. On rows of species presence (1 where a plot records a species) the cosine similarity is the Ochiai index of two species lists. The search is exact and computed in blocks, so memory stays bounded whatever the size of either set. It runs on the device reference is on; queries may stay in host memory and is moved over a block of rows at a time. With exclude_self=True, queries and reference are the same plots in the same order (pass the same tensor twice): plot i is never returned as its own neighbour, while another plot with the same species list still is. k is clamped to the reference size, one less with exclude_self. Returns (indices, similarities): (n_queries, k) int64 rows of reference and their float32 similarities, on the CPU.

rows = torch.from_numpy(presence.astype("float32")).cuda()
indices, similarities = rc.nearest_by_cosine(rows, rows, 50, exclude_self=True)

Scalers

The scaling fitted on the fitting plots, which a predictor applies to new plots: continuous_mean and continuous_scale (one entry per column of the continuous block), continuous_fill (the value a missing cell of each column reads as before scaling; None for a checkpoint written before missing cells were filled) and target_scalers (dict of regression target to its (mean, scale)).

predictor.scalers.target_scalers

RunMetadata

The run as a checkpoint records it, from Trainer.run_metadata or Trainer.load_run_metadata(path).

  • resolve_version (str), created_at, completed_at (str) and train_time_seconds (float).
  • n_plots_train, n_plots_test (int): the fitting and held-out plots.
  • hold_out (HoldOutMode), test_size (float, 0 for an explicit fold) and split_seed (int, the prepare_data seed, which also seeds the epoch shuffle).
  • best_epoch, total_epochs (int) and final_metrics (dict[str, dict[str, float]]).
record = rc.Trainer.load_run_metadata(path)
record.hold_out, record.n_plots_test

HoldOutMode

How a run’s held-out fold was drawn: Random (a test_size share of the plots, drawn with split_seed) or Explicit (the plots passed as stopping_indices).

dataset_config_from_checkpoint() 

dataset_config_from_checkpoint(schema, model_config)

The DatasetConfig a checkpoint was loaded with, rebuilt from its schema and model settings: species_encoding, hash_dim and top_k from the ModelConfig, because they size the model, and every other loader setting from the schema. use_cuda_hash is not restored. Predictor.dataset_config returns the same.

rc.dataset_config_from_checkpoint(predictor.schema, predictor.model.config).species_encoding

target_specs_from_schema() 

target_specs_from_schema(schema)

The targets a checkpoint was trained on, as TargetSpecs each reading the column of its own name: the targets a retrieval reference set is loaded with. The *_with_vocabs loaders replay the class codes.
